claims.statement: MultiRedisConfig in ecshopx-bootstrap hand-builds one LettuceConnectionFactory per logical Redis database (companys, springData, prism, datacube, deposit, members, espier, wechat) instead of relying on Spring Boot Redis auto-configuration, and its Javadoc states this exists so Docker/idle Connection reset is handled there via TCP keepalive plus validateConnection.

The shared helper standaloneFactory configures every factory with standalone-only RedisStandaloneConfiguration, socket keepAlive(true), configurable connect timeout, ClientOptions autoReconnect(true), a configurable command timeout, and setValidateConnection; the three knobs come from ecshopx.redis.lettuce.command-timeout (default 5s), connect-timeout (default 10s), validate-connection (default true).

Qualifier-to-logical-DB mapping: companysRedisTemplate (and the RedisTemplate<Object,Object> named redisTemplate) use ecshopx.redis.companys.database (default 0); springData-derived sharedStringRedisTemplate and dispatchBusStringRedisTemplate use spring.data.redis.database (default 0); prismRedisTemplate uses ecshopx.redis.prism.database (default 2); datacubeStringRedisTemplate uses ecshopx.redis.datacube.database (default 0); depositStringRedisTemplate uses ecshopx.redis.deposit.database (default 1); members/espier/wechat templates fall back to spring.data.redis.database when their ecshopx.redis.<name>.database key is unset.

Only the deposit, members, espier and wechat factories accept dedicated ecshopx.redis.<name>.host|port|password overrides with spring.data.redis.* fallbacks; the companys, springData, prism and datacube factories read host/port/password solely from spring.data.redis.*.

companysRedisTemplate is the @Primary StringRedisTemplate, so any StringRedisTemplate constructor parameter without @Qualifier resolves to the companys logical DB (e.g. AftersalesRefundSlowQueuePortImpl, StatementSettlementCursorRedisAdapter, OpenPlatformDispatchDedupeService); MerchantWxappLoginSmsVcodeAdapterConfig documents that merchant wxapp login SMS codes must instead inject @Qualifier("sharedStringRedisTemplate") for members-parity DB semantics.

sharedStringRedisTemplate and dispatchBusStringRedisTemplate are two separate qualifier beans built over the same springDataRedisConnectionFactory, so both land in the spring.data.redis.database logical DB; RedisDispatchDriver, RedisDispatchListener and RedisDelayedDispatchMover all inject the dispatchBusStringRedisTemplate qualifier, keeping dispatch:* queue keys in the shared/default DB.

DistributionConfigRedisReadService reads the distribution config from the companys DB under key distribution:config:<sha1(companyId)>, deep-merges the stored JSON over a default distributor structure, and tolerates missing/corrupt JSON by keeping defaults; DistributionConfigSetService is the matching write path (opsForValue().set of the same key). Goods' ItemsProfitSaveService never touches Redis directly: its applyDefaultProfitBranch (profit_type=0) first reads the category-level items_category_profit.profit_conf MySQL row, and only when that yields no usable popularize_profit does it call distributionConfigRedisReadService.getPopularizeSellerPercent as the fallback scale (percent ÷ 100, 4-decimal HALF_UP) written into the items table.

Order validity settings live in a hash key order_validity_setting with companyId as hash field, read by OrderValiditySettingRedisReadService (orders bundle) and OrderValidityPlatformSettingReadService (distribution bundle) — both on companysRedisTemplate and both merging their own DEFAULTS over the parsed JSON so a miss or parse failure degrades to defaults.

LanguageSettingRedisService persists company language settings in the companys DB under languageSetting:<companyId> through companysRedisTemplate with optimistic version-conflict checking on save, and loadSetting falls back to the default zh-CN-only setting both on a miss and on a Redis read or JSON parse exception (logging a warning in those cases).

Tenant settings stored in the companys DB (distribution config, order validity, language setting, payment-channel and ERP/logistics settings) have no MySQL write path in the Java code — their only persistence is Redis, where both compose stacks (docker-compose.dev.yml and docker-lite/docker-compose.yml) run redis-server --requirepass redispassword --appendonly yes --tcp-keepalive 60 with a persistent redis-data volume mounted at /data and a redis-cli PING healthcheck — so Redis is the system of record for them and FLUSHDB on that DB is configuration loss rather than cache invalidation.

Prism logical-DB state holds gateway/session credentials rather than tenant settings: H5JwtBlacklistService and OperatorJwtBlacklistService keep sha256-keyed JWT invalidation keys on prismRedisTemplate, CompanysActivationService keeps a 7-day black_token_<operatorId>_<operatorType> cache, and ShopexPrismSmsSignClient stores prism:<sha1(...)> access/refresh/forever tokens; SaaS-cert services also read certificates from the prism DB.

Deposit recharge writers use the shared/default DB, not the deposit DB: AdapayDepositTradeRechargeCallbackService increments the shopDepositTotal and dayRechargeTotal<yyyy-MM-dd> hashes (field companyId) via sharedStringRedisTemplate inside the @Transactional rechargeCallback, and addDepositToRedis runs only after a guarded conditional MySQL update (ECX-10915: UPDATE ... WHERE trade_status != 'SUCCESS' via LambdaUpdateWrapper.ne) wins — a zero update count or an already-SUCCESS row throws and no Redis counter is touched, preventing double counting from duplicate/concurrent callbacks. DepositTradeConsumeService mirrors it with decrements and dayConsumeTotal increments on the same shared template, and UserDepositBalanceMutationService writes the user_deposit MySQL row then refreshes the userDepositTotal_<companyId> hash (with MySQL fallback on hash miss).

The deposit day-counter is read through two different templates: DepositCountIndexReadService (admin RechargeController deposit count index endpoint) reads shopDepositTotal/dayRechargeTotal/dayConsumeTotal via sharedStringRedisTemplate (same DB as the writers), while CompanysDepositDayRechargeRedisReader.getRechargeTotal — feeding the dashboard real_deposit in CompanysDashboardStatisticsService — reads dayRechargeTotal via depositStringRedisTemplate, whose selector defaults to DB 1 while the shared DB defaults to 0, so the two indexes must be aligned per environment for real_deposit to be non-zero.

OrdersTradePaymentCallbackService allocates the daily tradeNo suffix from the shared DB on payment SUCCESS via nextTodayTradeSequence: it reads h_trade_no_<companyId>_<distributorId>_<MMdd> for an existing orderId, otherwise INCREMENTs c_trade_no_<companyId>_<distributorId>_<MMdd>, writes the mapping hash, and gives both keys a 24-hour TTL.

Day-scoped ID generators also live in Redis: DepositTradeIdGenerator builds CZ-prefixed deposit trade ids from the deposit_trade_id<yyyyMMdd> hash keyed by 90-second slots with a 24-hour TTL on the shared DB, while HfPayOrderApplyIdGenerator (hfpay_order_id/hfpay_apply_id counters with end-of-day TTL) and NormalOrderNumericIdService (<yyyyMMdd> hash keyed by 90-second slots) run on the companys DB.

Datacube tracking splits its Redis usage: TrackViewNumService increments datecube_tracklog:viewnum:<cid>|<monitorId>:page_view|unique_visitor|member_visitor:<sourceId> hashes (field yyyyMMdd) through datacubeStringRedisTemplate, while UvBloomFilterService's Lua GETBIT/SETBIT bloom filter (uv_bloom_filter:<monitorId>:<sourceId>) runs on sharedStringRedisTemplate, so UV dedup state and the counted hashes can be pointed at different logical DBs. Because the track endpoint is @FrontNoAuth, since ECX-10920 addViewNum silently returns — before any Redis or bloom-filter call — unless monitorId and sourceId are positive numerics that exist as Monitors/Sources rows for that company (monitorsMapper/sourcesMapper selectCount > 0), an anti-enumeration guard against unbounded key creation; TrackViewNumServiceMonitorScopeTest pins that unregistered or non-numeric ids produce zero Redis interactions.

WechatFansSyncService throttles fan syncs through membersStringRedisTemplate using a syncUsersCount<yyyyMMdd>:<sha1(companyId)> list capped at three pushes per day with a ten-minute minimum gap, expiring at end of day.

Adding a new logical Redis database requires editing MultiRedisConfig (a @Bean RedisConnectionFactory plus a @Bean StringRedisTemplate wired by @Qualifier) because the ecshopx.redis.*.database selectors are only consumed by @Value annotations inside that class — there is no generic registry — whereas repointing or collapsing existing areas is purely a per-environment override on the tracked selectors shipped in application.properties (spring.data.redis.database=0, ecshopx.redis.companys.database=0, ecshopx.redis.prism.database=2, ecshopx.redis.datacube.database=0, ecshopx.redis.deposit.database=1), applied via environment variables or CLI arguments such as the compose APP_ARGS block (which already overrides spring.data.redis.host|port|password but no database selector), because application-local.properties is git-ignored (.gitignore line 7) and therefore absent from fresh checkouts.

MultiRedisConfigLettuceFactoryTest is the only test of the wiring itself: it reflects the timeouts into a fresh MultiRedisConfig, calls standaloneFactory, and asserts getValidateConnection(), ClientOptions.isAutoReconnect() and socket keepAlive are all enabled; no test in the repo runs against a real Redis (consumers mock StringRedisTemplate/HashOperations).

ShopadminDeferredOrderCache persists the operator-side deferred order on sharedStringRedisTemplate instead of a MySQL row: the shopadmin create flow (order_type=normal_shopadmin, ShopadminNormalOrderCreateOrchestrator.create) writes a JSON ShopadminDeferredOrderSnapshot under shopadmin:deferred:<companyId>:<orderId> with status WAIT_PAY and a TTL taken from the auto_cancel_time delta (15-minute fallback when absent or in the past); later failure states (PAID_WAIT_ORDER, REFUNDED, REFUND_FAILED) rewrite the snapshot with the 24-hour COMPENSATION_TTL_SECONDS; a Redis read failure throws ResourceException while a corrupt JSON blob reads as a null miss; and payment of such an order id is routed back into the deferred flow by NormalOrderAdminPaymentService when no order_associations row exists.

ShopadminDeferredOrderCache.withLock serializes the deferred-order pay/materialize/refund transitions with the shopadmin:deferred:lock:<orderId> key: setIfAbsent with a random UUID token and a 120-second TTL, refusing the action (订单处理中，请稍后查询) when the lock is not acquired, throwing on Redis failure during acquisition, and releasing via a best-effort token-checked unlock that deletes the key only if it still holds this caller's token.

Wxapp mini-program sessions live in the shared DB: WxappMemberAuthService.resolveSession reads session3rd:<token> (JSON with open_id/union_id/session_key) through sharedStringRedisTemplate and throws UnauthorizedException on a miss or corrupt JSON, so flushing the shared DB logs out every mini-program user.

Member SMS verification codes live in the members DB: MemberSmsVerificationCodeDeliveryService writes member-<type>:company<companyId>:<mobile> (TTL 300 s) through membersStringRedisTemplate and rate-limits sends with a yzmsend:<companyId>:<yyyyMMdd>:<type>:<mobile> counter (24 h TTL, capped by common.sms-send-limit, default 5, rejecting with 验证码发送过多).

Operator-side captcha and SMS codes live in the companys DB: OperatorsImageVcodeService stores 4-char image captchas under admin-<type>:<token> with 300 s TTL and deletes the key on a successful case-insensitive check; OperatorSmsVerifyService stores operator-sms:verify:<type>:<mobile> (180 s TTL) and forget-password codes under admin-forget:<mobile> (300 s TTL), all via companysRedisTemplate.

Fast-buy cart state is split across two DBs: member fast-buy snapshots go to fastbuy:<sha1(companyId+userId)> JSON with 600 s TTL on the shared DB (WxappH5CartAddService.setFastBuyCart, cart_id forced to 0), while operator (shopadmin) fast-buy state goes to shop_fastbuy:<sha1(companyId:operatorId:distributorId)> JSON with 600 s TTL on the companys DB (OperatorShopFastBuyRedisService, forcing cart_id=0 on every set and degrading missing/corrupt blobs to an empty map; OperatorCartFastBuyFacadeImpl accumulates num only when the stored item matches).

The self-pickup verification flow spans two logical DBs: orderziticode:<code> → orderId mappings (1800 s TTL) are written to the shared DB by OrderZitiQrCodeRedisService and consumed by AdminOrderQrWriteoffService/CommunityChiefQrWriteoffService via resolveOrderIdOrThrow (throwing 核销码已过期 on a miss), while phone-scoped admin-pickupcode:<orderId>|<phone> codes (1800 s TTL) are written to the companys DB; OrderPickupSmsRedisVerifyService.verifyAndConsumePickupCode checks the companys-DB key first (with loose numeric comparison), falls back to the shared-DB code→order mapping, and on success deletes both keys so a code cannot be redeemed twice.

Goods-arrival subscriptions mirror the durable subscribe_notice MySQL rows (sub_status NO → SUCCESS) with a shared-DB Redis hash for the mini-program UI flag: keys from GoodsArrivalNoticeSubscribeRedisKeys.hashKey are arrivalNoticeSub:<companyId>:<itemId>[:<distributorId>] for source wechat and arrivalNoticeSub:<source>:<companyId>:<itemId>[:<distributorId>] otherwise, with userId hash fields holding JSON {open_id, wxa_appid}; subscribing toggles both stores, and GoodsArrivalSubscribeMatchService.markSuccess deletes the hash fields after the arrival notification is sent.

MultiRedisConfig declares exactly ten named template beans mapped to six logical DB selector groups: companysRedisTemplate (@Primary, ecshopx.redis.companys.database default 0) and redisTemplate over companysRedisConnectionFactory; sharedStringRedisTemplate and dispatchBusStringRedisTemplate over springDataRedisConnectionFactory (spring.data.redis.database default 0); prismRedisTemplate (ecshopx.redis.prism.database default 2); datacubeStringRedisTemplate (ecshopx.redis.datacube.database default 0); depositStringRedisTemplate (ecshopx.redis.deposit.database default 1); and members/espier/wechat templates whose database selectors fall back to spring.data.redis.database — the shipped application.properties pins shared 0, companys 0, prism 2, datacube 0, deposit 1.

EmployeePurchaseEmailVcodeRedisService runs on the explicitly qualified sharedStringRedisTemplate (spring.data.redis.database, default DB 0) and stores employee-purchase email verification codes at employee-purchase-email:<email> with a caller-supplied TTL (1800 s from EmployeeEmailVcodeSendService); verifyAndConsume compares the stored code and deletes the key on match, giving one-shot semantics, and EmployeeCheckService.doEmailBranch rejects a mismatch with "验证码错误".

The employee-purchase email vcode send path enforces three Redis throttles on the shared DB before sending: a per-email cooldown key employee-purchase-email-cd:<companyId>:<email> with 60 s TTL checked via hasKey, a per-email daily counter employee-purchase-email-day:<companyId>:<yyyyMMdd>:<email> rejected past 5 sends, and a per-IP daily counter employee-purchase-email-ip:<companyId>:<yyyyMMdd>:<ip> rejected past 200; both daily counters use Asia/Shanghai dates and receive their 24-hour EXPIRE only when INCR returns 1, so the window is fixed rather than sliding.

PassphraseBehaviorRateLimitService (ECX-10917) protects the unauthenticated passphrase behavior-report endpoint with a fixed-window INCR counter on the shared DB under ep_behavior_rl:<companyId>:<activityId>:<enterpriseId>:<subject>, where subject prefers u<userId>, then v<visitorKey>, then ip<clientIp> (literal ipunknown when all are absent); the first increment of a window sets EXPIRE 60 s and a count over LIMIT_MAX=10 throws TooManyRequestsException, which GlobalExceptionHandler maps to HTTP 429.

PassphraseBehaviorReportService.report invokes the rate limiter before loading the activity or writing any behavior-log row, so over-limit unauthenticated reports produce zero MySQL writes; the limiter fails open because it only acts on the non-null Long returned by INCR.

The wider employee-purchase Redis family also lives on the shared DB: PassphraseVerifiedRedisService stores verified flags at ep_passphrase_verified:<companyId>:<activityId>:<enterpriseId>:<userId> with an activity-end-derived TTL clamped to [1 h, 90 d]; PassphraseParticipateQuotaRedisService keeps remaining quota at ep:pquota:<companyId>:<activityId>:<enterpriseId> consumed atomically by a Lua GET/DECR script; EmployeePurchaseFastBuyRedisService mirrors the member fast-buy cart at employee_purchase_fastbuy:<sha1(companyId+enterpriseId+activityId+userId)> with a 600 s TTL and forced cart_id=0; EmployeePurchaseInviteRedisService tracks share-invite tickets in the employee_purchase_invite:<companyId> hash, locking a code by moving its field to <code>_.

EmployeePurchaseEmailVcodeRedisServiceRateLimitTest pins the 60 s cooldown TTL and the 24-hour expiry set only on the first daily increment, while PassphraseBehaviorRateLimitServiceTest pins the 10-per-60 s window, the TooManyRequestsException past the limit, and first-hit window TTL — both against mocked StringRedisTemplate/ValueOperations with no real Redis.
